scope: Design gate for ptest NG: docs/designs/2026-09-17-ptest-ng-design.md and docs/plans/2026-09-17-ptest-ng.md audited against the user-approved docs/specs/2026-09-17-ptest-ng-product.md, .pipeline/context.md, AGENTS.md, the three research inputs, and the actual repository (legacy `ptest`, `tests/`, absent packaging). Read-only; no tests, edits, installs or shell execution.
coverage: Checked: spec-to-design traceability for P1-P4, S1-S4, T1-T5, D1-D4, C1-C3, section 7 resource contracts, section 10 bounds/security axes, A1-A14 and the milestone gates; CLI grammar/JSON schema/enum precision; config and env precedence including PTEST_* rejection and runner-side (PYTEST_ADDOPTS/VITEST_*) bounding; serial-without-xdist path; admission/FIFO/exclusivity/memory accounting; guard registration CAS, cancellation, quiescence proof and crash recovery; fixture-domain and nested-invocation rules; baseline/input identity, non-input outputs, changed-during-run semantics, failure obligations; doctor bounds/no-execution/prompt boundaries; retention and quota caps; task ownership disjointness, wave ordering, frozen helper interface, the legacy-bootstrap barrier (verified line-by-line against the installed legacy dispatcher's source in this repo), and the T13 deletion inventory against the real file tree. NOT checked: no tests, linters, builds or benchmarks were run (docs gate); filesystem permissions/ownership of ~/.local/state/ptest and ~/.config/ptest could not be stat'ed (no shell); existence/contents of pinned third-party versions (psutil 7.2.2, Bandit 1.9.4, pip-audit 2.10.1, Gitleaks 8.30.1, pytest 9.1.1, xdist 3.8.0, Vitest 3.2.7) and of the adoption repos/commits could not be verified offline; upstream pytest/xdist/Vitest API behaviour was accepted from the research doc rather than re-derived; the cx-ng-foundation prototype worktree was not inspected; legacy cloud tests, outsource_tests.md and docs/superpowers/* were only enumerated, not read.

blocking.issue: The NG normal-domain state root is byte-identical to the legacy ptest state root, and the design specifies no behaviour for pre-existing legacy directories/contents while requiring strict 0700 private-directory validation before creating state.
blocking.location: docs/designs/2026-09-17-ptest-ng-design.md §7 (first paragraph: "Linux roots: <account>/.config/ptest/machine.toml and <account>/.local/state/ptest"; "Validate owned private directories (0700), regular files (0600) … before creating state"; "No version suffix or alternative production root") vs ptest:74-75, ptest:712, ptest:746-748
blocking.evidence: Legacy defines `CONFIG = Path(os.environ.get("PTEST_CONFIG", Path.home()/".config/ptest/config.toml"))` and `STATE = Path.home()/".local/state/ptest"`; `ACTIVE = STATE/"active"` and `registered_run()` calls `ACTIVE.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)` on every local run, creating `~/.local/state/ptest` and `~/.local/state/ptest/active` with the process umask (0755 under the usual 022) and 0644 JSON records inside it. The design's NG state root is that same path, and `~/.config/ptest/` is the same directory the legacy install guide populates via `cp config.example.toml ~/.config/ptest/config.toml` (0644). Traced failure: a user (or this project's own developer machine, where the plan's bootstrap wrapper invokes the installed legacy ptest for every task's tests and keeps re-creating `active/`) runs `ptest --full` after installing NG; `domain_paths()` resolves the shared root, the scheduler's pre-creation validation observes a 0755 directory containing foreign 0644 files and, per §7, must fail closed ('Scheduler corruption/unavailability stops execution; it must not fall back to unlimited independent launches'). Result: NG cannot execute at all for exactly the migrating population P4 and A1 target, and the T14 final self-hosted gate plus A12 adoption runs (which use the normal domain) cannot run. The alternative implementer reading — silently chmod 0700 a directory legacy is concurrently writing to — is also unspecified and mutates legacy state. The scheduler research (docs/research/2026-09-17-scheduler-feasibility.md, 'Domain and storage' table) proposed `<account-home>/.local/state/ptest/coordination/`; the design collapsed it to the bare root without recording why, and macOS keeps a `state/` child, so the two platforms are already asymmetric.
blocking.whyItFailsDoD: Spec P4 permits side-by-side legacy installation and requires migration to work on machines that ran legacy ptest; A1 requires fresh install/init smoke on supported platforms and byte-identical preservation of existing config; A12 requires independent adoption. A first-run fail-closed on every legacy machine defeats all three, and the design gate exists to freeze this location.
blocking.fix: Freeze the NG coordination root as a dedicated child that cannot pre-exist from legacy (e.g. Linux `<account>/.local/state/ptest/coordination/`, matching the research recommendation and the macOS `state/` child), and state explicitly in §7 that (a) the NG root is created by NG with 0700, (b) pre-existing sibling legacy entries under `~/.local/state/ptest` and `~/.config/ptest` are ignored and never counted toward NG quotas, pruned, or rejected, and (c) `machine.toml` validation applies to the file, not to a shared parent directory that legacy or the user created. Add an A1 negative fixture that pre-creates a 0755 `~/.local/state/ptest` with a legacy `active/<pid>.json` and asserts NG still initialises and executes.

blocking.issue: The frozen unknown-memory policy combined with the frozen config default makes every stock repository serialise the whole host to one job, contradicting S3, and the spec-mandated benchmark of that policy is absent from both design and plan.
blocking.location: docs/designs/2026-09-17-ptest-ng-design.md §5 (`memory_mb_per_worker = 0 # 0 means unknown, not free memory`) and §7 ("Unknown memory estimates allow at most one unknown-memory job at a time"); §12 performance paragraph; docs/plans/2026-09-17-ptest-ng.md 'Frozen test-helper interface' final sentence and Task 14 measurement step
blocking.evidence: Init writes `memory_mb_per_worker = 0` and §5 gives no mechanism by which init estimates memory, so every freshly initialised repository is 'unknown'. §7 then caps concurrency at one unknown-memory job at a time, unconditionally (the sentence adds 'configured memory reservations and global job/slot limits still apply', i.e. this is an additional, not alternative, constraint). Traced outcome: with the frozen defaults (`slots=min(4,max(1,floor(usable_cpus/2)))`, `jobs=min(2,slots)`), two agents in two different checkouts of two different repositories can never run concurrently — the second queues behind the first for its entire setup+execution+publication lease. That directly contradicts spec S3 ('Different checkouts may run concurrently within the shared budget') and the I2 premise the product exists for. The plan confirms the effect rather than the intent: 'Concurrency fixtures declare known tiny memory estimates so unknown-memory serialization does not make admission tests vacuous' — so A2/A3/A4 are all exercised on a configuration no real user will have, and the default behaviour is never tested end to end. Separately, spec S2 ends 'The design must specify the unknown-estimate policy and benchmark it on simultaneous Python/Node fixtures'; the design specifies the policy but §12's performance list (20 warm wrapper samples, plan 10k, doctor 2k/16MiB, 5 alternating adoption pairs) and plan T14's measurement step contain no simultaneous Python/Node concurrency benchmark, and the scheduler research's 'Benchmark the conservative unknown policy and explicitly document its throughput cost' is unaddressed.
blocking.whyItFailsDoD: Violates S3's concurrency contract and leaves an explicit S2 design obligation ('must … benchmark it on simultaneous Python/Node fixtures') undelivered, while the acceptance fixtures deliberately avoid the default configuration, so A2's admission evidence does not cover shipped behaviour.
blocking.fix: Either (a) make unknown memory non-blocking by default — rely on slot/job ceilings, and apply the one-unknown-job rule only when `machine.toml` declares a `memory_mb` budget (state this conditionality explicitly in §7) — or (b) have `init` record a conservative per-runner default estimate so stock repositories are 'known'. Whichever is chosen, add the S2-mandated benchmark to design §12 and plan T14 (simultaneous pytest+Vitest fixtures, unknown vs known estimates, throughput cost published), and add one A2 case that runs at the shipped defaults rather than with injected tiny estimates.

blocking.issue: The frozen shared contract omits the write-side and default-value primitives that four disjointly-owned tasks each require, forcing independent reimplementation of the security-critical exclusive/no-follow creation and atomic publication paths with no route to consolidate them later.
blocking.location: docs/designs/2026-09-17-ptest-ng-design.md §6 signature list (only `read_regular` is exported from files.py) and §6 note 'Local private helpers may differ; inter-task names/types may not'; docs/plans/2026-09-17-ptest-ng.md Task 0 'Produces' and step 3 ('safe exclusive writes and atomic owned-file publication as local helpers'), Global constraints ('contracts.py and its generated schema descriptors are the one shared authority. No worker invents another public signature'), Task 9 test example using `DEFAULT_SCAN_LIMITS`
blocking.evidence: The design requires exclusive no-follow creation and/or atomic owned publication in at least four separately owned modules: §5 'File creation uses exclusive no-follow open' (config.py, T1), §11 'Atomic private outcome creation is fsync+rename within owned directory' and per-checkout history store (history.py, T3), §7 `domain.json`/marker/bootstrap.lock creation and validation (scheduler.py, T4), §4 '`--result-json` and `guide --write` … output creation is exclusive, never overwrites an existing file' (operations.py/cli.py, T11), plus the fixture-domain marker in T0's own helper. §6 exports none of them, and both the design and the plan forbid depending on another task's unfrozen names, so each owner must write its own version. Traced consequence: five implementations of the same O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW + fsync/rename + ownership/mode-validation boundary, each needing its own A8/A11 negative fixtures; a defect found in one (say, a missing final fstat after open, which §10 requires for doctor but no other module) cannot be repaired centrally because disjoint ownership forbids editing another task's file, and the plan's security-axis map assigns 'input' only to T0/T1/T8/T11 and 'state' to T3/T4/T7/T11, so the divergence is not even uniformly tested. The same gap exists for constants: plan Task 9's red test calls `inspect(resolve_config(root), DEFAULT_SCAN_LIMITS, None)`, but `DEFAULT_SCAN_LIMITS` appears in no §6 record or signature, so T9 and T11 (CLI defaults) must each invent it. The guard control/manifest protocol (§7 'Control protocol 1 messages are bounded length-prefixed JSON …') is likewise a cross-task interface (T7 produces, T11 consumes) that is absent from the contract catalog; that one is at least sequenced safely, but it is not frozen.
blocking.whyItFailsDoD: M1's exit gate is 'frozen config/CLI/JSON/resource contracts … and bounded owned tasks'; the plan's own rule that contracts.py is the single shared authority is unsatisfiable when the primitives four owners need are explicitly declared local. Spec section 10's Input/State axes demand one validated boundary, not four.
blocking.fix: Before the T0 barrier, add to design §6 (and to T0's 'Produces') the write-side and default primitives with exact signatures and owners — e.g. `create_exclusive(path, data, mode) -> None`, `publish_atomic(directory, name, data) -> Path`, `validate_private_dir(path) -> None`, `validate_private_file(path) -> None` in files.py, and `DEFAULT_SCAN_LIMITS: ScanLimits` in contracts.py — and state that T1/T3/T4/T11 must consume them rather than reimplement. Add the guard control/manifest frame descriptor to the same catalog (protocol=1, bounded lengths, message enum) so T7 and T11 cannot diverge.

blocking.issue: `ptest register [--json]` is in the frozen CLI grammar but has no document kind, payload, schema descriptor or enum membership in the frozen JSON contract.
blocking.location: docs/designs/2026-09-17-ptest-ng-design.md §4 grammar line `ptest register [--json]` vs §6 'Public JSON version 1' ("`kind` is init/plan/where/status/history/doctor/run", "`PublicDocument` is the tagged union of the seven public payloads") and the 'Other payloads' list, which has no register entry
blocking.evidence: §4 accepts `register --json`; §5 says 'register prints a redacted migration/config preview without writing'; spec C2 requires that pure inspection `--json` produce one valid versioned document, including errors, and spec P4 requires `register` to provide the migration/init preview. But the frozen envelope enumerates exactly seven kinds and PublicDocument is closed over seven payloads, and `scripts/export-schemas.py` generates `docs/schemas/v1/*.json` from those descriptors with a drift test. Traced failure: T11 implements `register --json`, must emit a `kind` value; any value it picks is either outside the strict enum (the strict codec and the consumer's 'required fields/types/enums are strict' rule reject it) or silently overloads `init`, which the design never authorises, and the generated schema set has no descriptor to validate against, so the drift test passes while an undocumented document ships.
blocking.whyItFailsDoD: Breaks C2 ('The design freezes schema IDs, required fields, outcome/reason/error enumerations … before coding') and section 8's 'No unused placeholder command is advertised as implemented' for a command the grammar exposes.
blocking.fix: In §6 either add an eighth `register` kind with its payload fields (redacted legacy mapping, proposed runner/commands summary, warnings, required adoption action) and a generated schema, or delete `--json` from `register` in §4 and state that the machine-readable migration preview is `init --dry-run --json`. Record the choice in the reason-code/enum catalog so T11 and the drift test agree.

blocking.issue: Exact single-patch acceptance tuples make an untested runner *version* an execution-blocking `unsupported-capability`, so ordinary repositories lose first-class execution and fall back to a profile that reserves the entire host budget exclusively — a cooperation regression against the legacy dispatcher.
blocking.location: docs/designs/2026-09-17-ptest-ng-design.md §3 profile table ("pytest 9.1.1; xdist 3.8.0 optional; pytest-cov 7.1.0 and coverage 7.15.0") and the paragraph after it ("A differing runner or critical plugin version is `unsupported-capability` for that first-class profile until its matrix is added"; "The user can deliberately adopt `command` … Reserves the entire shared slot budget and one job exclusively")
blocking.evidence: The design draws no distinction between an untested version and an unsafe configuration, even though the same paragraph asserts 'Execution capability and selection capability are separate: unsupported selection evidence causes full; unsafe execution configuration errors before tests'. Traced failure: a repository pinned to pytest 9.1.0 with no xdist configured requires *no* version-specific behaviour at all on the design's own serial path ('With no xdist and valid serial config, pass no `-n` and no `-p no:xdist`'), yet it is refused; the documented remedy is the `command` profile, which per §3 and §7 'takes exclusive budget and starts only with zero active jobs'. Six agents on one workstation therefore drop from legacy's per-run cap (legacy `ptest:386` injects `-p no:xdist` or `-n N` for any pytest version) to strict one-at-a-time whole-host reservation. The plan corroborates the adoption cost: T14 must pick `marshmallow-code/apispec` specifically because its lock is asserted to carry pytest 9.1.1, and `dcastil/tailwind-merge` must be *modified* ('isolated derivative dependency alignment to Vitest/coverage 3.2.7') to become testable — i.e. neither adoption candidate exercises an unmodified real-world repository.
blocking.whyItFailsDoD: Spec section 2 requires unsupported versions to 'lose the affected capability explicitly', not to lose basic execution, and explicitly forbids requiring an optional parallelization plugin merely to execute serially when a tested serial path exists; A12 requires fresh adoption of independent repositories without silently upgrading them.
blocking.fix: Split the matrix in §3 into (a) tested tuples that unlock worker bounding, native inventory and selection, and (b) a compatible-range execution policy (e.g. pytest 9.1.x / coverage-configured, Vitest 3.2.x) that still permits bounded serial execution with `capability.selection=false` and an explicit `unsupported-capability` limitation reason, rejecting only configurations the adapter cannot bound (xdist present at an untested version, custom pools, remote transports). State the degradation rule and add a negative fixture: untested-patch runner + no parallel plugin ⇒ serial execution at grant 1, not exit 2.

blocking.issue: The installation contract stops at 'build the wheel, swap a symlink' and never specifies how the installed bundle obtains its runtime dependency (psutil) or whether installation requires network, leaving T13 unable to implement A1's interruption/rollback property deterministically.
blocking.location: docs/designs/2026-09-17-ptest-ng-design.md §12 ("Local installation uses an explicit destination and a versioned private bundle, builds/validates the wheel first, then atomically changes a same-directory symlink with Python os.replace") and §3 ("Runtime dependencies: Python stdlib plus `psutil==7.2.2`"); docs/plans/2026-09-17-ptest-ng.md Task 13 step 2
blocking.evidence: A wheel is not executable and the design names no environment-construction step, while NG — unlike legacy, whose README states 'No dependencies beyond Python 3.11+' — now requires a compiled third-party package. Traced failure: T13's owner must invent the mechanism (private venv built with uv at install time? vendored psutil? `uv tool install`?), which the plan's escalation rule forbids ('do not repair an impossible … promise with hidden private APIs … or a new subsystem'), and each choice has a different interruption profile, so `test_failed_upgrade_keeps_old_target` cannot be written against a frozen contract. On an offline machine the unspecified step fails outright, and P1's 'documented isolated installation' plus the context-level requirement that network needs be explicit are unmet.
blocking.whyItFailsDoD: P1 requires a documented isolated installation and an interrupted upgrade that leaves either the prior or the new complete installation usable; A1 tests exactly that. The design gate is supposed to freeze the bundle layout before T13 codes it.
blocking.fix: Freeze in §12 the bundle layout and dependency provisioning: e.g. `<dest>/ptest-<version>/` containing a private virtual environment built from the validated wheel plus the pinned psutil wheel, with the dependency source (local wheel cache vs index, and whether network is required) stated explicitly, the symlink target named, and the completeness marker the installer writes last. Add the offline/no-network installation case and the partial-bundle-then-interrupt case to T13's tests.

blocking.issue: The frozen 300-second default queue deadline turns ordinary contention on the target workstation into `75` 'no tests ran' outcomes, and silently overrides the research recommendation without recording a reason.
blocking.location: docs/designs/2026-09-17-ptest-ng-design.md §7 ("Queue default timeout 300s, accepted 1–3,600s") vs docs/research/2026-09-17-scheduler-feasibility.md 'Recommended finite defaults' table ("Queue deadline | Default 30 min, finite validated maximum 24 h")
blocking.evidence: Defaults are `jobs=min(2,slots)` and — per finding NG-2 — effectively one concurrent job for stock configurations. Traced scenario using the product's own reference numbers (legacy README: persea-api full run ~3 min): three agents launch runs within a minute of each other; the third waits behind two leases of ~4 minutes each (setup + execution + publication, all inside the lease), exceeds 300 s and receives exit 75 with no tests executed. This is the routine case on the six-agent workstation the product exists for, and 75 is documented as 'temporary scheduling … unavailability', inviting retry loops that re-enter the back of a strict-FIFO queue. The design records no rationale for departing from the research default.
blocking.whyItFailsDoD: S3 requires that queued work be admitted fairly and that a deadline produce a scheduling error rather than a false pass; a default that fires during normal cooperative use converts the scheduler's core value into frequent non-execution, and section 11's performance/acceptance evidence never measures queue-wait distribution.
blocking.fix: Raise the default queue deadline to the researched 1800 s (keeping the validated 1–3600 s range, or extend the maximum), or justify 300 s in §7 with the contention model it assumes. Either way, add a queue-wait observation to `status`/result `timings` reporting and one A3 case asserting that a run behind two full-length predecessors is admitted rather than timed out at the shipped default.

blocking.issue: The frozen example configuration violates the design's own `project_id` domain rule.
blocking.location: docs/designs/2026-09-17-ptest-ng-design.md §5 example (`project_id = "cd58ec6cf99748ce9f15dfce137f044d3"`) vs §5 field domains ("`project_id` is exactly 32 lowercase hex characters") and the comment on the same line ("generated 128-bit hex at init")
blocking.evidence: The literal is 33 characters (cd58/ec6c/f997/48ce/9f15/dfce/137f/044d = 32, plus a trailing `3`). A 128-bit value is 32 hex characters. Traced failure: T1 builds `tests/ng/fixtures/config/` from the frozen example, the validator T1 also writes rejects it with `invalid-config`, and the worker must decide whether the example or the rule is authoritative — precisely the ambiguity the contract freeze is meant to remove. The same string is a natural template for the `PTEST_PROJECT_ID` 32-hex environment contract in §10 and the `pt_<checkout8>_<run32>_…` prefix length arithmetic.
blocking.whyItFailsDoD: M1 requires frozen, self-consistent config contracts; section 8/C2 require strict field domains. An example that fails its own validator is a defect in the frozen artifact.
blocking.fix: Correct the §5 example to a 32-character lowercase hex literal and add a T1 fixture asserting that a 31- and a 33-character `project_id` are both rejected with `invalid-config`.

blocking.issue: The Task 9 red-test example contains an assertion that cannot fail, while the traceability matrix credits that test toward A8's 'no-findings is never displayed as certified parallel safety' negative case.
blocking.location: docs/plans/2026-09-17-ptest-ng.md Task 9 step 1 (`assert report.readiness[1].state != "certified"`); design §6 `Readiness` record and §10 readiness states
blocking.evidence: `Readiness.state` is frozen to `ready-for-declared-capability|blocked|unknown`; `"certified"` is not a member of the enum and the record validates on construction, so the assertion is true for every possible report and can never detect a regression. The index-based `readiness[1]` also assumes an ordering that §6/§10 never freeze (areas are execution/parallel/selection/timing but no order is specified), so the line is simultaneously vacuous and order-fragile. Traceability row A8 lists T9 as an owner for 'No-findings is never displayed as certified parallel safety'; as written, that obligation is satisfied by an assertion with no failure mode.
blocking.whyItFailsDoD: audit-spec and spec A8 require negative cases that can actually fail; a tautological assertion is false evidence in the acceptance matrix.
blocking.fix: Replace with an assertion that can fail against the real contract, e.g. select the parallel readiness entry by `area` rather than index and assert `state == "unknown"` with a `scan-limit`/hypothesis reason present for a project containing no detectable pattern, plus a rendering assertion that the human/JSON output for that state contains no certification wording. Freeze the readiness ordering in design §6 if tests are to rely on it.

notes: Bootstrap barrier verified against the real legacy dispatcher and it works as claimed: `PTEST_CONFIG` is read at ptest:74; `resolve_project` (ptest:226-248) matches the stanza by `source_repo()` = `--git-common-dir` parent, so the plan's `root = /absolute/git-common-dir-parent` is correct from any worktree, while `root = git_root(cwd) or cwd` (ptest:2754) keeps execution in the *current* worktree, satisfying the barrier's '`where` must show the current worktree'; `--local` sets `force_local` (ptest:2744); `workers=1` yields `-p no:xdist` (ptest:386), which is a harmless no-op when xdist is absent; and `refuse_disguised_full` cannot fire for the plan's file-list invocations because only directory arguments qualify (ptest:528-533). Caller args are `shlex.quote`d (ptest:2814) so `-k` expressions stay literal.

The T13 deletion inventory matches the actual tree exactly: all 20 listed `tests/*.py` files plus `tests/conftest.py` exist and nothing else lives in `tests/`; the four `Dockerfile.*`, four `cloudbuild.*.yaml`, `scripts/spot-worker-startup.sh` and all ten terraform files exist as listed. `.gcloudignore` is the one cloud-only artifact in the tree that neither design §12 nor plan T13 mentions — decide explicitly whether it stays as history or is removed with the rest.

Plan Task 6 owns `tests/ng/fixtures/vitest/package-lock.json` pinned to Vitest/coverage-v8 3.2.7 but states 'npm dependency installation is requested through candidate ptest setup after T11, not hand-installed', and no step authorises generating the lock. `npm ci` (the design's setup recipe) requires the lock to already exist, so add an explicit, reported lock-generation step (e.g. `npm install --package-lock-only` in the fixture directory under the authorised dependency-setup allowance) or T6 cannot deliver its owned fixture and T11's Vitest native_cli gate is blocked.

Plan Task 14 says 'Use normal admitted domain for substantial adoption runs, one at a time' while the final step says 'Every nested acceptance child uses an explicit validated fixture domain'. These are only compatible if the normal-domain adoption runs are driven by `scripts/acceptance.py` invoked directly by root and never by a test collected into the final self-hosted `ptest --full`; otherwise those tests nest in the same domain and return 75/`nested-invocation` during the single final gate. State that constraint explicitly in T14 and in `tests/ng/test_acceptance.py`'s scope.

Plan Task 5 lets the pytest bridge import the trusted `contracts` module from its installed path inside the *project's* interpreter, but neither design §3 nor §5 freezes a supported project-interpreter range (the 3.11-3.14 target reads as ptest's own interpreter). If an adopted project's venv predates that range, the bridge fails with a syntax/import error rather than a clean `unsupported-capability`. Either freeze the minimum project interpreter for the pytest profile or prefer the design's second option (ship the generated protocol descriptor alongside the bridge) so the bridge carries no dependency on ptest's language level.

design §10 sets doctor's `elapsed` limit to 5 s, which is exactly the spec's p95 performance target for the same 2,000-file/16 MiB bound. The latency target therefore cannot be violated — a slow reference machine produces truncated reports instead of a measurable miss. Consider a deadline above the target (e.g. 8 s cap against a 5 s p95 target) so the benchmark retains signal, or state in §12 that the doctor latency target is measured as 'completed without hitting the elapsed cap'.

Plan Task 11 owns 'package directory `__init__.py` files where needed' while Task 0 owns `src/ptest/__init__.py`; the overlap is unstated. Also confirm T0's packaging declaration covers package data that later tasks create (`ptest/runtime/vitest_bridge.mjs`, `ptest/resources/agent-guide.md`, `ptest/resources/recipes/*.md`) and the `ptest/adapters`/`ptest/runtime` subpackages, or T13's wheel build will ship an installable CLI with a missing bridge.

history.py (T3) and scheduler.py (T4) each stand up an independent SQLite store with pragma verification, bounds and corruption handling. The two-database split is correct per design §9, but the connection/pragma/quota helper is duplicated across disjointly-owned modules with separate A14 corruption fixtures; consider freezing one small shared helper alongside the NG-3 primitives.

The frozen helper `case.invoke(..., timeout=10)` default is tighter than several contracts it will be used to test (30 s recovery target, 300 s default queue deadline, 600 s compound probe cap, per-attempt 30 s). Callers can override, but the default invites flaky watchdog kills in shadow/probe tests; consider a default aligned to the fixture's expected phase plus an explicit override in every lifecycle test.

Third-party pins could not be verified offline: psutil 7.2.2, Bandit 1.9.4, pip-audit 2.10.1, Gitleaks 8.30.1, pytest 9.1.1, xdist 3.8.0, pytest-cov 7.1.0, coverage 7.15.0, Vitest/coverage-v8 3.2.7, Node 26.8.2, Go 1.27.1, Cargo 1.98.1, and the apispec/tailwind-merge commits. The design-author record already flags the Vitest and adoption risks; treat the rest as unverified until T0/T13 resolve them and report actual resolved versions.

Positive observations worth preserving: the guard registration CAS-before-execution ordering, provisional-facts-until-quiescence rule, `killpg(pgid,0)` ESRCH proof with charge retained on EPERM/uncertainty, and the refusal to signal stored PIDs together give a genuinely fail-closed S4; the PTEST_CONFIG leak between the legacy bootstrap and candidate children is handled on both sides (helper clears it, plus a deliberate retain-and-reject negative case); the `pt_<checkout8>_<run32>_<attempt4>_<worker4>` prefix is exactly 54 ASCII as stated; probe repeat range 1-5 x 2 attempts matches the a001-a010 attempt-id domain; and the generated-from-descriptors JSON Schema with a drift test correctly avoids a second hand-maintained schema source.
reviewed_files: repository file tree (root scripts, Dockerfiles, cloudbuild configs, terraform/, docs/superpowers/)
